title: GOP senator warns Anthropic of "alarmist" approach to AI
source_used: Senator Bernie Moreno's own press release and letter (https://www.moreno.senate.gov/newsroom/press-releases/moreno-blasts-anthropic-ceo-for-hypocritical-approach-to-super-intelligence/), The Next Web (https://thenextweb.com/news/bernie-moreno-letter-dario-amodei-anthropic-alarmist) and Seeking Alpha via TradingView; Axios's own page was not readable
key_facts: On Monday 5 Oct 2026 Republican Senator Bernie Moreno of Ohio sent a letter to Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei; his office published it as a press release.

Moreno wrote that Anthropic's recent actions and statements reflect an 'alarmist approach' that puts extraordinary emphasis on the most catastrophic outcomes of AI (the letter calls AI 'super intelligence', or SI).

He called it hypocritical to plan a stock-market listing and ask Americans to invest while warning the product could lead to their extinction; he cites investors discussing a valuation near $2 trillion, about 42 times revenue, and trading expected as soon as October 2026.

He cites Jacob Coxon, who quit Anthropic and accused Anthropic and OpenAI of 'gambling with our lives'; Anthropic safety researcher Evan Hubinger saying the chance AI kills all humans within a decade is over 10%; Amodei telling CNN he agrees with Coxon 'on far more than I disagree with him'; and a 25% chance of SI going 'really, really badly' that he attributes to Amodei.

Moreno urged Amodei to focus on how AI can strengthen US national security and counter attacks by adversaries, said addressing the risks 'does not require halting its development or surrendering American technological dominance', and called Amodei's signature on the White House accord on super intelligence 'a notable first step'.
The Next Web says Axios first reported the letter and that it is the latest from an ally of President Trump aimed at Amodei.
Seeking Alpha says 'super intelligence' is the term the US federal government now uses for artificial intelligence.
quote_evidence: I do not understand how you can ask them to invest their hard-earned savings in Anthropic’s continued development while warning those same Americans that your product could ultimately lead to their extinction.
Anthropic’s recent actions and statements reflect an alarmist approach to SI that places extraordinary emphasis on the technology’s most catastrophic outcomes.
why_it_matters_hint: A sitting senator is publicly challenging how loudly an AI company warns about extinction risk just as it prepares to sell shares to the public.
notes: Axios's page returned a Cloudflare block (403). Facts come from the senator's own press release and full letter, The Next Web (which says Axios first reported the letter) and Seeking Alpha via TradingView. The letter says trading is expected as soon as October 2026; Bloomberg (5 Oct edition item 5) reported a roadshow from 9 Nov and a listing in mid-November, so the listing date is not settled and is left out of the entry.
